name: Acronym Formulation & Disclosure
description: Scrutinizes the protocol by which acronyms are introduced, expanded, and sustained across a document.
algorithm: Entity Protocol Mapping & Acronym Distance Tracker
mechanism: Commercial AI models exhibit a pathological adherence to the 'Introduce and Expand' protocol. Regardless of the target audience's presumed expertise, if an AI mentions 'NASA' or 'CEO' for the first time, it has a high statistical probability of aggressively spelling it out as 'National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)' or 'Chief Executive Officer (CEO)'. This stems from RLHF alignment enforcing clarity and accessibility. Human experts writing for other experts deliberately assume shared knowledge, routinely dropping acronyms without explanation. This tool maps the introduction of every acronym, calculating the ratio of aggressively expanded acronyms against 'orphan' unexpanded acronyms to detect the hallmark of AI over-explanation.
parameters:
Analysis: Document-Level Entity Tracing
Metric: Acronym Expansion-to-Orphan Ratio
Output: 0-100 Over-Clarification Score
accuracy: Moderate — 65-75%, highly dependent on the implied target audience of the text.
source: Pragmatic linguistics and LLM alignment safety research.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated B2B whitepapers, technical documentation, or medical articles that awkwardly 'over-explain' industry-standard acronyms to an expert audience.
strengths:
• Explores a behavioral alignment quirk (over-helpfulness) rather than just a grammatical pattern.
• Extremely effective on niche, highly technical texts where human authors would naturally skip definitions.
• Computationally light; utilizes simple regex and entity tracking.
limitations:
• Easily defeated if the prompt specifies 'assume the reader is a PhD expert, do not explain acronyms'.
• Generates false positives on highly formal bureaucratic or legal documents where exhaustive acronym definition is a strict human requirement.
• Meaningless on casual texts or short posts lacking complex terminology.

references.title: Ouyang, L., et al. (2022). Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback. NeurIPS.
